newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one stories.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one stories.

text.p: WASHINGTON - Saying that "mistakes were made" in the pursuit of campaign contributions, President Clinton told reporters that a top financial regulator should not have been invited to a coffee party arranged by the Democratic National Committee for bankers who contributed to the party.

WASHINGTON - Del. Eleanor Holmes Norton said it would be "immoral" for congressional representatives from the Maryland and Virginia suburbs to oppose her plan for deep income tax cuts in the District because they have blocked a commuter tax and left the city struggling for survival.

PORT ELIZABETH, South Africa - The killers of anti-apartheid activist Steve Biko were identified, ending nearly two decades of mystery about who murdered one of the nation's most charismatic opponents of white-minority rule.

TESANJ, Bosnia - As Bosnian Moslem army soldiers spread out to practice defending a snow-covered hill, Bob Oberlender, a retired U.S. army sergeant, moved among them, advising where to set up machine guns, where to aim rifles and what to do if a squad member gets shot.

WASHINGTON - The Labor Department reported that overall wages and benefits continued to rise only modestly during the last three months of last year, prompting a wild swing in the stock market and easing fears that Federal Reserve policy makers would raise short-term interest rates next week.

WASHINGTON - The president of a large mental health contractor in the District spent corporate funds on mink coats, weddings, investments in a golfing magazine and campaign contributions to D.C. Mayor Marion Barry before her firm was forced out of business last year.
RICHMOND - Virginia senators voted to retire "Carry Me Back To Old Virginia" as the official state song.
